findings.reason: it adds one refusal clause and one done-when case (a live fenced run whose home carries no entry) and the property is checkable directly by reading the run home's settings.json, so the node should refuse on the fact rather than on its proxy.
findings.text: §8 refuses `crew tell` on "a live run whose record does not say `fenced: true`", treating the fence flag as proof that the run home carries the `PostToolUse` entry; a fenced Claude-dialect run launched before this section lands carries `fenced: true` and a settings.json seeded without the entry, and nothing re-seeds a live run's home (`seed_harness_home` is called from launch composition only, `reckon/_backends.py:2383`, gated on `adopts_harness_home = fence` at `:2379`), so `crew tell` would answer `queued_for_next_tool_call`, the message would sit unclaimed, and the section would reproduce §1's silent non-delivery one hop later — the exact outcome its own sentence says it refuses in order to prevent

findings.reason: the deliverable's own instruction is "create the run home's `settings.json` when the loop produced none", which yields the right file under either reading of it, so only the explanatory sentence is imprecise and no node would be sent down a wrong path.
findings.text: the sentence "an operator with no `~/.claude/settings.json` gets no run-home settings at all" is false in the ordinary fenced Claude dispatch: `_seed_worker_mcp_settings` (`reckon/_worker_fence.py:317-338`) writes `<run home>/settings.json` whenever `worker_mcp_servers` is not `None`, which is every launch composed from a resolved flight config, so the file exists with the MCP keys and no hooks even when the operator has no settings file
